'Inspections tab links and buttons, phone use, and the inspection's asset
'Yes
'The tab no longer has a filter row, and it now follows a work order when its asset is changed or assets are merged, instead of staying on the asset first inspected.

'Phone: the rule 'The filter row will wrap on a phone rather than scrolling out of view, and will keep its counts' is deleted, because the tab has no filter row. Asset: before (22 Sep spec), the asset was 'stored on the inspection when it is created rather than derived through its work order ... this tab is a record of what was inspected rather than a view that follows a later correction', so after changing a work order's asset the inspection stayed on the old asset's tab. Now (14 Oct spec): 'The tab lists the inspections whose work order is on this asset now, so it follows the work order when the work order's asset is changed or two assets are merged.' It moves to the new asset's tab and leaves the old one.

'S5-R16: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S5-R10: 5 Oct 2026 (Developer and QA questions answered)
S5-R21: 5 Oct 2026 (Developer and QA questions answered)

'The filter row wraps on a phone rather than scrolling out of view, and keeps its counts.
An inspection records the asset it was run on, stored on the inspection at creation rather than derived through its work order, and pre-release inspections are backfilled from their work order's asset at migration.

'The tab has no filter row, so on a phone there is no filter row to wrap.
The tab lists the inspections whose work order is on this asset now. When a work order's asset is changed, its inspections move to the new asset's Inspections tab and leave the old one.
When two assets are merged, the inspections move to the surviving asset, as the work orders do.

'2. On a phone, confirm every column's information stays reachable and the page does not scroll sideways; the filter row wraps and keeps its counts.
3. Confirm the tab shows what was inspected (asset stored on the inspection at creation), not a view that follows a later work-order asset change; confirm a pre-release inspection was backfilled from its work order's asset.

'1. On a phone, open the asset's Inspections tab.
2. Check there is no filter row.
3. On desktop, open the work order of one inspection and change its asset to another asset.
4. Open the new asset's Inspections tab and check the inspection is listed there.
5. Open the old asset's Inspections tab and check the inspection is no longer listed.
6. Merge two assets of the same customer (for example by editing one asset's VIN to the other's and answering Yes to merge).
7. Check the inspections of both are listed on the surviving asset.

'Decided on 5 Oct. The 22 Sep spec said nothing about merging assets; under its rule an inspection stayed with the asset it was run on. Not covered here: a later product manager ruling (8 Oct, not yet in the 14 Oct spec) that an inspection whose work order is deleted takes the asset that work order has at that moment. Pre-release inspections being listed on their work order's asset, and every column staying reachable on a phone, are unchanged and are left out.

'How findings are counted, once per axle
'No
'The Needs action filter step 4 checks no longer exists; the counts are now followed by the tab's summary line instead.

'Before (22 Sep spec): the counting rule said 'the asset list, the report summary and the Needs action filter all follow it', and step 4 of the case checked that filter. Now (14 Oct spec): 'the asset list, the report summary and the summary line on the tab all follow it', and 'The table has no filter row.' The counts themselves come out the same; the only difference a tester sees is that the Needs action filter is gone and the summary line takes its place.

'S5-R10: 5 Oct 2026 (Developer and QA questions answered)
S5 counting note: 7 Oct 2026 (Filter leftovers removed)

'There is no Needs action filter on the asset's Inspections tab.
The asset list, the report summary and the summary line on the tab ('N of M have findings with no lines yet') all follow the same counting.
'4. Confirm the asset list, report summary and Needs action filter all follow this same count.

'Steps 1 to 3 of the case are unchanged.
4. Open the asset's Inspections tab for these inspections.
5. Check there is no Needs action filter on the tab.
6. Check each row's findings match the counts you confirmed in steps 1 to 3.
7. Open each inspection's report and check its summary shows the same counts.
8. Read the summary line 'N of M have findings with no lines yet' and check it agrees with these inspections.

'The case's Expected results have no line for step 4; the old expectation is in the step itself. This is a knock-on of removing the filter row on 5 Oct; the counting rules give the same counts as before. Separate from this change: the precondition 'some hidden fields' cannot be met in either version and should be fixed when the case is rewritten.

'Inspections tab with not-started, all N/A, deleted, moved and many inspections
'Yes

'After the run-on work order is deleted, only an inspection with a report is kept, as a read-only record that can no longer be built from, reopened or regenerated; a reopened one shows as Completed and opens its latest report.

'Before (22 Sep spec): 'the inspection remains listed, the work order column shows a dash rather than a broken link, and the row remains usable' - an unfinished inspection stayed listed, a kept row could still be built from onto a new work order, and a reopened one read In progress. Now (14 Oct spec): 'an inspection that has a report stays ... as a read-only record ... It cannot be built from, reopened or regenerated. A reopened inspection survives as its latest report: Status reads Completed, Completed shows the date of that report, and opening the row opens that report ... An inspection with no report ... is deleted with its work order.' The unfinished one is gone, the kept row is read-only with View PDF only, and a reopened one reads Completed and opens its report.

'S5-E3: 6 Oct 2026 (Deleted work orders, removed inspections and splits)
S3-R6: 7 Oct 2026 (Deleted work order: outcome, footer, reopened, merge (SV-10965))
SV-10965: 7 Oct 2026 (Milos Vasic in Jira)
'If the run-on work order has been deleted, the inspection stays listed, the work order column shows a dash rather than a broken link, and the row stays usable.

'Only an inspection that has a report (completed, or completed and then reopened) stays listed on the asset's Inspections tab after its work order is deleted. One with no report, such as an unfinished one, is deleted with the work order.
The kept row is a read-only record: it cannot be built from, reopened or regenerated, and its completed screen offers View PDF only.
The Action column shows the outcome (for example 'WO created S-200') only while the work order it points to still exists; otherwise it shows a dash.
A reopened inspection shows Status 'Completed' with the date of its latest report, and opening the row opens that report rather than the answers.
If the lines went onto a different work order and that work order is deleted while the work order the inspection was run on still exists, the row returns to Needs action and offers the build action again (unchanged).

'3. Delete the run-on work order and confirm the inspection stays listed with a dash in the work order column and remains usable; delete a different work order the lines were built onto and confirm the row returns to Needs action.

'1. On one work order for this asset, complete one inspection with a Not OK finding, complete and then reopen a second, and leave a third unfinished.
2. Delete the work order.
3. Open the asset's Inspections tab.
4. Check the completed and the reopened inspections are still listed, each with a dash in the Action column, and the unfinished one is gone.
5. Check the reopened one reads Completed, with the date of its latest report.
6. Open the completed one and check it is read-only and its footer offers View PDF only: no Build lines, no Reopen and no way to regenerate the report.
7. Click the reopened one's row and check its latest report opens, not its answers.
8. On a different work order for this asset, complete an inspection with a Not OK finding, press Build lines, choose A new work order and press Add Lines.
9. Delete the work order that inspection was run on (not the new one).
10. On the asset's Inspections tab, check that row shows 'WO created …' in the Action column, linking to the new work order.
11. On a work order you keep, complete another inspection with a Not OK finding, press Build lines, choose A new work order and press Add Lines.
12. Delete the new work order that got the lines.
13. On the asset's Inspections tab, check that inspection's row needs action again: its Action column offers the build action.

'Product manager decisions of 6 and 7 Oct; the developer built it on 8 Oct. The spec also deletes an inspection that was submitted but whose report was never generated; that state cannot be produced by hand, so it is left out. The last check (lines put on another work order that is then deleted, while the inspection's own work order still exists) is unchanged and is kept so the case does not lose it.

'Build lines from a needs-action row, with the same work order choice
'Yes
'A work order that cannot take lines is now left out of the menu instead of being listed with a reason.

'Before (22 Sep spec): 'When it is not [eligible], the target keeps its place and says why', so the menu listed the Complete work order, greyed out with a reason. Now (14 Oct spec): 'When it is not, it is not offered', and the change log says 'a target that cannot be used is not shown'. The Complete work order is absent and only 'A new work order' is listed.

'S6-R4: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S2-R15: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
S2-R5: 29 Sep 2026 (QA contradiction pass answered)
'The run-on work order is offered as a target only while it is an eligible build target (judged by its status on the row); when it is not, the target keeps its place and says why.

'When the row's work order is not eligible (for example Complete), the menu still opens but does not list that work order at all - not greyed out and with no reason given; it offers only a new work order.
'3. Check the run-on work order is offered only while its status is eligible; when it is not, the target stays listed and says why.

'1. On the Needs action row whose work order is Complete, press the build action.
2. Check the menu opens and offers only a new work order, with no entry for the Complete work order.

'Decided on 29 Sep. On 22 Sep the Complete work order already could not be chosen; the only change is that it is no longer shown at all. The eligible work order being listed by number and status is unchanged and is left out.

'After building, the row shows the result and the counts update
'No
'There is no Needs action filter any more; after a build the row shows its outcome and the summary line updates.

'Before (22 Sep spec): 'the row will leave the Needs action filter and the counts and summary will update with it', and the summary read 'N of M need a work order'. Now (14 Oct spec): 'the row will show its outcome instead of the action, and the counts and the summary line will update with it'; there is no filter row and the summary reads 'N of M have findings with no lines yet'. The row showing its outcome after a build is not new.

'S6-R7: 7 Oct 2026 (Filter leftovers removed)
S5-R10: 5 Oct 2026 (Developer and QA questions answered)
'After a successful build, the row leaves the Needs action filter and the counts and summary update with it.

'There is no Needs action filter for the row to leave.
After a successful build the summary line, which reads 'N of M have findings with no lines yet', updates with it: N goes down by one.
'3. Confirm the row leaves the Needs action filter and the counts and summary update with it.

'1. Open the asset's Inspections tab and check there is no Needs action filter.
2. Note the summary line 'N of M have findings with no lines yet'.
3. Build from the Needs action row and press Add Lines.
4. Return to the asset's Inspections tab.
5. Check N in the summary line has gone down by one.
'A knock-on of removing the filter row (5 Oct) and the new summary wording. The row showing its outcome instead of the build action is unchanged and is left out.
